title: Marswalk shelters and safe points
description: Places the route planner can send the crew to when an event starts. The habitat comes first. Natural safe points come from the sky view of the terrain. Field definitions are in public/data/README.md, the method is in docs/route/shelters.md. Built by scripts/build-shelters.mjs; do not edit by hand.
frame: x east, z south, metres from Cheyava Falls (engine frame, same as route.json)

tags.DATA: Measured by a mission or a lab study, or stated in a NASA specification or procedure. The provenance block names the document and the page.
tags.DERIVED: Calculated by us from DATA values. The note gives the calculation.
tags.SIM: Our own assumption or game choice. The note says why and what it is based on.

protection.full: Closes the hazard: the crew can stay as long as needed.
protection.partial: Lowers the hazard but does not stop it. Planner fallback when no full shelter can be reached.

sky_view.method: Ray cast on the 751 x 751 height grid: 48 azimuths, rays to 400 m or the tile edge, dose point 1 m above the ground. Visible fraction = mean over azimuths of (1 - sin(horizon elevation)), horizon clamped at 0.

shelters.name: HAB · habitat airlock
shelters.reason: Pressurised habitat. Inside the crew has air, power and walls between them and the sky. It is the only shelter that protects from every event.

position.unit: m (x east, z south, from Cheyava Falls)
position.label: HiRISE DEM · habitat placement

provenance.site: Jezero crater, Neretva Vallis, around Cheyava Falls
provenance.reference: Habitat placement rule in src/engine/habitat.js (habitat.init) and the airlock geometry in public/marswalk/assets_habitat/habitat.json
provenance.locator: habitat.json, airlock: "outer hatch faces +X; sill 1.02 m above the ground at x = 7.23; the steps reach the ground at about x = 9.9"
provenance.note: Foot of the airlock steps. The engine places the habitat on the flattest spot within 30 m of the HAB waypoint (520, 600): centre (541, 582), 0.26 m of relief under the 11 m footprint, airlock turned toward the first waypoint. The steps reach the ground 9.9 m from the habitat origin along that heading. build-shelters.mjs repeats the rule on the same height grid.

shelters.name: SP1 · terrain shade
shelters.reason: Walkable ground where the terrain hides 15 % of the sky, next to the route. The horizon rises to 28 deg toward azimuth 355 deg. Use it to wait out a solar particle event only when the habitat is too far. It gives no protection from a dust storm or low oxygen.

provenance.site: Jezero crater, Neretva Vallis, around Cheyava Falls
provenance.reference: Marswalk terrain tile public/marswalk/assets/terrain.json (751 x 751 heights, 2 m spacing, from the HiRISE 1 m DEM of Jezero crater); sky view computed by src/sim/skyView.js through scripts/build-shelters.mjs
provenance.license: HiRISE products are NASA/JPL/University of Arizona, public with no restriction of use (NASA SPD-41A).
provenance.note: Sky view 0.846 of the upper hemisphere at 1 m above the ground (72 azimuths, rays to 400 m), against 1.000 on open flat ground and a tile median of 0.927. Assumes an isotropic SEP flux above the horizon: dose is proportional to the visible solid angle of the upper hemisphere, and the planet blocks everything below the horizontal. The real flux at the surface is stronger toward the zenith, because particles arriving at a low angle cross more atmosphere, so blocking the low sky saves less than this estimate. Read the reduction as an upper bound. It ignores secondary particles from the ground and the rock itself (albedo neutrons) and the galactic background, which comes from the same sky.
